109: They were obligated in ḥalla but they were not obligated in tithes - From Sifrei, Parashat Shelach: As it is written, "upon your coming to the land whither I bring you there" [Numbers 15:17]. Scripture varied this "coming" from all the other "comings" in the Torah. For in all the other instances it is written "And it shall be when you come", whereas here it is written "upon your coming." [Sifrei Bamidbar 110:1]  When they entered the land they were [immediately] obligated in ḥalla, but they were not obligated in tithes until after inheritance and settlement, as is written, "You shall set aside every year a tenth part" [Deuteronomy 14:22] and subsequently is written "in the place where [God] will choose" [Deuteronomy 14:23] -- they were not obligated until Shiloh was chosen. That is, after the conquering and dividing as is written in Joshua.  Throughout the time of conquering and dividing, the Tent of Meeting was in Gilgal -- for fourteen years, as is stated in Zevachim. [Zevachim 118b:13]
